focus: The setting is a Beach Umbrella and Two Chairs. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.

answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.SAND: Sand consists of small loose grains. A pebble is much larger than an individual grain of sand.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.HAT: A hat covers the head. The brim projects outward, while the crown is the part above it.
answerNotes.SHELL: Shell means a hard outer covering. The same everyday word can describe the outside of an egg, nut, or crab.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.

answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.FISH: Fish live in water and breathe through gills. A seal or otter swims too, but it is a mammal rather than a fish.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.SCREEN: Screen can mean a display surface or a mesh barrier. The phone and movie scenes use the display meaning; a porch door uses the mesh meaning.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.SHORE: Shore is land at the edge of water. It can border a lake as well as the sea.

Dark time between sunset and dawn

answerNotes.FLAME: A flame is the visible burning region above fuel. A glowing ember is hot too, but it does not necessarily have a flame.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.TENT: A tent is a portable shelter made from fabric and supports. Its poles hold the shape while pegs or other anchors secure it.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.

answerNotes.ZOO: A zoo displays and cares for animals. A keeper is a person responsible for animal care, not the name of an enclosure.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.TICKET: A ticket can give admission or identify an item left for a service. A theater ticket and a dry-cleaning claim ticket serve different uses.
answerNotes.GATE: A gate opens through a fence or other boundary. Hinges let it move, and a latch holds it closed.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.

answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.TICKET: A ticket can give admission or identify an item left for a service. A theater ticket and a dry-cleaning claim ticket serve different uses.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.MUSIC: Music can be played by instruments or sung. A concert is an event at which music is performed, rather than the music itself.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
